titre: every one of these has a source 🧠 #adhd #adhdtiktok #neurodivergent #adhdcheck #fyp
notes: Format « faits » (9f4fd230, 857,6 k), en mythe / vérité. Accroche neuve : « ADHD myths people still believe ». Sources : (1) 1798, Alexander Crichton, « An Inquiry into the Nature and Origin of Mental Derangement » (Palmer & Finger, Child Psychol Psychiatry Rev, 2001) ; (2) persistance à l'âge adulte (Faraone et al., World Federation of ADHD International Consensus Statement, Neurosci Biobehav Rev, 2021 ; Song et al., J Glob Health, 2021) ; (3) héritabilité ~74 % (Faraone & Larsson, Mol Psychiatry, 2019) ; (4) hyperfocus rapporté plus souvent par les adultes avec TDAH (Hupfeld, Abagis & Shah, ADHD Atten Def Hyp Disord, 2019) ; (5) critère DSM-5 : symptômes dans au moins deux contextes et gêne réelle (APA, DSM-5, 2013) ; (6) ~5 % des enfants, sur tous les continents (Polanczyk et al., Am J Psychiatry, 2007) ; (7) 1 713 personnes avec TDAH et 1 529 sans, 3 242 IRM, petites différences moyennes de volumes sous-corticaux (Hoogman et al., Lancet Psychiatry, 2017). Aucun médicament, aucune mort.

slides.texte_overlay:
myth: ADHD is a new trend.

truth: a scottish doctor
described it back in 1798

myth: you grow out of it.

truth: for many people
it carries on into adulthood

myth: it's caused by bad parenting.

truth: genes play a big role.
twin studies put it at about 74%

myth: people with ADHD
can't focus.

truth: many adults with ADHD
describe hyperfocus on the things
that grab them

myth: everyone is a little ADHD.

truth: a diagnosis needs symptoms
that cause real problems
in more than one part of life

myth: it's just an american thing.

truth: it's found all over the world,
in around 1 in 20 kids

myth: it's just personality.

truth: a 2017 study of over
3,000 brain scans found small
average differences in the brain

follow for more ADHD myths,
with sources
